macros.name: arbcolor
macros.doc: arabluatex provides its own \arbcolor command which is able to render syllabes or diacritics in colors.

macros.name: ArbOutFile
macros.doc: \ArbOutFile[⟨newline⟩]{⟨string⟩} silently exports ⟨string⟩ to the external selected file.

macros.name: arind
macros.doc: \arind{⟨root⟩} is a command specialized in the contruction of indexes.

macros.name: ayah
macros.doc: \ayah{⟨number⟩} prints up to 3-digit numbers inside ‘end of Ayah’ sign (U+06DD) or inside parentheses depending on the mode which is selected.

macros.name: bayt
macros.doc: The arabverse environment and the \bayt command are designed to typeset the verses in a two-column, fixed width layout.

macros.name: LR
macros.doc: \LR{⟨arg⟩} is designed to typeset its argument from left to right.

macros.name: MkArbBreak
macros.doc: The \MkArbBreak{⟨csv list of commands⟩} command can be used in the preamble to give any command—either new or already existing—the precedence over arabluatex inside Arabic environments.

macros.name: newarbmark
macros.doc: \newarbmark lets the user define additional Arabic marks.

macros.name: NoArbUp
macros.doc: \NoArbUp may be used either in the preamble or at any point of the document in case one wishes to have the tanwīn on the line.

macros.name: prname
macros.doc: \prname is to be used outside Arabic environments for proper names. It takes as argument one or more Arabic words, each of which will be rendered in upright roman style with its first letter uppercased.

macros.name: RL
macros.doc: \RL{⟨arg⟩} does the same as \LR{⟨arg⟩}, but typesets its argument from right to left.

macros.name: SetInputScheme
macros.doc: The input scheme, which is set to arabtex by default, may be changed at any point of the document by the \SetInputScheme{⟨scheme⟩} command, where ⟨scheme⟩ may be either arabtex or buckwalter.

macros.name: setLR
macros.doc: \setRL and \setLR can be used to change the direction of paragraphs, either form left to right or from right to left.

macros.name: SetTranslitConvention
macros.doc: The transliteration mode, which is set to dmg by default, may be changed at any point of the document by the \SetTranslitConvention{⟨mode⟩} command , where ⟨mode⟩ may be either dmg, loc or arabica.

macros.name: SetTranslitFont
macros.doc: \SetTranslitFont{⟨font selection command⟩} allows any specific font to be selected for rendering transliterated text with the font-selecting commands of the fontspec or luaotfload package.

macros.name: txarb
macros.doc: \txarb sets the direction to right-to-left and selects the Arabic font.

macros.name: uc
macros.doc: Proper names or book titles that must have their first letters uppercased may be passed as arguments to the \uc{⟨word⟩} command.

macros.name: Uc
macros.doc: \Uc does the same as \uc except that it is never discarded.

envs.name: arabexport
envs.doc: The arabexport environment processes and prints its argument unchanged to the current .pdf file. Additionally, if arabluatex is loaded with the export option, this argument is exported to the external selected .tex file with Unicode in place of the original arabtex or buckwalter strings.

envs.name: arabverse
envs.doc: The arabverse environment and the \bayt command are designed to typeset the verses in a two-column, fixed width layout.
